[agent-bulk] shw 5019 (305.6 MeV, 5 seg, pdg 11, len 103.5) is OVER-CLUSTERED: it has swallowed a straight minimum-ionising stem. Its five members are the cluster-5 vertex piece 5019 (11.3 cm) + 5011 (10.5 cm) + 5012 (5.0 cm) at 5.3 cm / 14.2 deg - about 27 cm in total - and then TWO long cluster-45 segments, 45029 (29.8 cm, reco pdg 13) at 16.2 cm / 10.6 deg and 45030 (46.8 cm, reco pdg 13) at 44.5 cm / 10.1 deg, both pulled in by pass3_cone. That is 77 cm of a DIFFERENT cluster, both pieces PID'd as tracks, making up three quarters of the object's length. On shw5019-az-055-el+20 that 77 cm runs off to the left as one thin straight line whose point cloud stays roughly 3 cm wide from end to end; on shw5019-az+085-el+20 the same member set resolves into TWO separate narrow lines diverging by about 20 deg, not one cone. A 200+ MeV electromagnetic cascade cannot stay 3 cm wide for 77 cm - the yellow set spans two directions and one of them is a track. Marked 45029 and 45030 OUT. Both marks are the same strength: they are two halves of one continuous track and the owner reverses them together. Consequence worth stating: if they come out, 5019 is a ~27 cm vertex EM object and its 305.6 MeV is mostly track charge run through the shower hypothesis. VERTEX IS GOOD, judged from vtx-az-055-el+60 (event_half_span_cm 112.3, no --vtx-span re-capture needed): the star is a clean three-way junction and the two long unowned prongs 5001 (pdg 2212, 102.1 cm) and 5017 (pdg 13, 37.6 cm) both touch it at 0.00 cm and are correctly left grey. NOTHING IS MISSING from 5019: shw5019-acc shows four member squares (5011 and 5012 coincide) and NOT ONE non-member circle inside 58 cm; the nearest non-member, 5009 (11.0 cm), is at 154.6 deg, i.e. behind the start. So this is over-clustered only, not 'both'. THE READING I REJECTED: a converted photon does give two narrow prongs from a common origin at a small opening angle, and 20 deg is in that range - so 'correct, this is an early e+e- pair' is not absurd. I rejected it on width and length: the long prong keeps a constant ~3 cm cloud for 77 cm and never branches or fans, and 103.5 cm total is far beyond the visible extent of a 305 MeV cascade. Speculation the owner may want to test: the 77 cm cluster-45 track may be this numuCC event's actual muon, in which case the muon has been absorbed into the EM shower. NO PI0: the reconstruction stored none and I propose none - the only other shower nodes are nine fragments at 6.1 MeV and below (12020, 22025, 13021, 24027, 20023, 23026, 46031, 21024, 19022, three of them flagged 'conn 4: dropped by the PF tree'), all out of scope and not looked at as objects.

VERTEX IS ACCEPTABLE: the star sits at the apex of the EM fan, which is what a nuecc vertex should look like. THE VERDICT IS GENUINELY CLOSE AND I RECORD IT AS unclear. The single question is 14024: 7.1 cm, cluster 14 (the SAME cluster as the shower), reco pdg 11, 10.9 MeV, conn 1, TOUCHING the shower (dist 0.00) and touching the main vertex (0.00 cm) - and it is its own separate shower node rather than a member of 14025. On shw14025-az-055-el+20 it is drawn green and reads as one more prong of the same fan leaving the same apex. READING A, under-clustered (what I recorded): it is contiguous, same cluster, same vertex, EM PID, and 14025 ALREADY accepts a sibling at essentially the same angle - its own cmp_div says its six members span 0.0-16.7 cm and 0.0-56.3 deg, and member 14026 sits at 77-83 deg from the vertex. Taking 14026 and leaving 14024 is the asymmetry that bothers me. Marked 14024 IN. READING B, correct: I measured 14024 myself against a PCA axis of the six members (the display reports it as dist 0 / angle 0 because it touches, so the table cannot answer this) and it spans r 0.0-6.7 cm at 82-116 deg from the vertex - i.e. part of its extent lies BEHIND the shower start, about 3 cm behind and 6 cm sideways, and nothing in a shower goes behind its start. What breaks the tie for neither side: at r under 7 cm the angle-from-vertex measure is nearly meaningless - a 6 cm transverse offset at 6.7 cm radius is 60 deg by construction - which is exactly why I cannot separate the two readings. THE MARK IS THE ONE I WOULD MOST WILLINGLY LET THE OWNER REVERSE, and the stake is small either way: 10.9 MeV against 122.2. Reconciliation check (correction 11): nseg 6 and exactly six segments carry owner 14025, so 14024 is genuinely a non-member and not a shared segment. NOTHING ELSE IS MISSING: every other non-member within 50 cm is at 50-174 deg and sub-1 cm apart from 44017 (2.2 cm at 88 deg) and 46019 (4.7 cm at 147 deg, behind); there is no unowned charge on the axis beyond the members' 17.8 cm reach. NOT over-clustered: single apex on both azimuths. WORTH THE OWNER'S EYE SEPARATELY: segment 14001 is a 413.7 cm pdg-13 track in cluster 14 - one of only two clusters carrying this neutrino candidate - and it terminates about 5 cm from the main vertex. At 4 m it is far more likely a cosmic that got merged into the candidate cluster than anything from this interaction. The reconstruction does leave it UNOWNED (in_main_cluster walk_exclude), which is right, but its presence in the candidate cluster at all is a clustering question one level above this scan. NOT LOOKED AT: 10 of the 11 shower nodes were out of scope at 15.3 MeV and below (44017, 14024, 47020, 39012, 46019, 43016, 22011, 41014, 40013, 45018), except that 14024 is the subject of this verdict. [agent-bulk] other_em. shw 26021 (105.2 MeV, 4 seg, pdg 11, len 25.3) is UNDER-CLUSTERED, and separately this event has an event-level oddity the owner should see. CLUSTERING: on shw26021-az-055-el+20 the yellow member set is a proper cone - the X at the top, the fan widening away from it down the orange axis - and it ends at 17.6 cm. About 5 cm past the last member, sitting ON the axis right at the tip of the axis arrow and drawn in its own purple, is 97017: 2.9 cm long, 13.5 MeV, at 22.6 cm / 9.8 deg, tier 1. Nothing about the star is misplaced; what is wrong is the association of a 2.7 m distant blob with it. That is a clustering question one level above this scan, so I state it rather than voting on it. NO PI0 and none proposed. The display's auto-slotted pair 26021 + 22009 prices at 89.0 MeV on the axis convention and 42.0 MeV on the vertex convention, but pairing two objects 2.5 m apart as one pi0 is not physical and I did not store it. NOT LOOKED AT: 4 of the 7 shower nodes were out of scope at 13.6 MeV and below (25010, 97017, 93015, 98018), except 97017 which is the subject of the mark above. Also not judged as objects: 22009 (32.9 MeV) and 96016 (28.5 MeV), which are in scope but not the verdict shower - both sit near the vertex and I saw nothing obviously wrong with either in the close-in vertex frames.
